children: Apple Inc. (AAPL) shares fell about 1.5% in premarket trading after reports of a touchscreen MacBook and a separate report that iPhone 18 Pro component orders were cut by roughly 15%.

Apple (AAPL) opens iPhone Duo preorders Oct 16; shipments start Oct 23. Analyst warns early supply limits may push customer waits to about five weeks, complicating early demand assessment.
Early China data: iPhone 18 Pro sales strong. Apple (AAPL) held 33% of China smartphone market in Week 38. Duo-related demand remains a key outlook factor for traders.
AAPL slipped ~1.9% premarket after a report warned of supply‑chain impacts. Traders watch supplier ties (TSMC, Qualcomm, Broadcom, Amkor, Corning, TI) and upcoming supply data for clarity.
Apple (AAPL) plans limited initial production of its foldable iPhone Duo at about 8–10 million units this year; manufacturing may not ramp quickly enough to hit that range.
Apple (AAPL) raised Pro model prices by $100 worldwide. Traders note higher memory costs tied to AI demand may pressure iPhone demand and consumer uptake of new models.
Apple names John Ternus CEO; Tim Cook becomes executive chair, shifting to government relations, global policy, and strategic support as company prepares for a major product cycle.
Apple (AAPL) plans its first touchscreen MacBook, reportedly unveiled October 27 with an updated iPad mini; additional MacBook Pro and iMac updates are slated later in the month.
Apple (AAPL) is expected to use OLED displays in next‑gen MacBook Pro. Analysts forecast OLED notebook shipments rising 50% in 2026 and 24% in 2027, boosting premium laptop OLED adoption.
